newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran spends $118 mln on air traffic control radars.
newsitem.headline: Iran spends $118 mln on air traffic control radars.

text.p: Iran is spending $118 million to boost its air traffic control by expanding radar coverage throughout its airspace, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Monday.
Iranian media have said the project was being carried out with French cooperation, but have given no further details.

IRNA quoted Ali Shahcheraghi, head of Iran's civil aviation authority, as saying $80 million had been spent on setting up ten radar stations and another 114 billion rials ($38 million) had been allocated to buy additional radar equipment.
Shahcheraghi said the plan included building two air control centres and raising the number of air corridors to 67 from 23, the agency reported. He did not say when the project would be completed.
